label: prf:binding-genfun-qdifference
title: Proof of the q-difference recurrence of the binding generating function
html:
Write G(x;q)=\sum_{n\geq 0}B_n x^n and R(q,x)=\sum_{j} r_j(q)\,x^{j} with j ranging over a window of width d. Comparing the coefficient of x^{n+d} on both sides of G(qx;q)=R(q,x)G(x;q), the left side contributes q^{n+d}B_{n+d} and the right side a finite \mathbb{Q}(q)-linear combination of B_{n},\dots,B_{n+d}. Solving for B_{n+d} (the coefficient r of the top power is a unit in \mathbb{Q}(q)) yields the depth-d recurrence B_{n+d}=\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}a_j(q)\,B_{n+j} with a_j rational in q and the r_j. This is the standard fact that a q-holonomic series has P-recursive coefficients; it fixes every term — and hence the growth law \rho\cdot A — from the first d terms and R.

For the Archimedean image, apply \tau at q=q_0 and let q\to q_0 act on the shift operator x\mapsto qx: the multiplicative q-shift degenerates to the infinitesimal generator x\,\partial_x (the confluent limit of a q-difference operator), so G(qx;q)=R(q,x)G(x;q) passes to a linear differential equation x\,\partial_x \widehat{G} = \rho(x)\,\widehat{G} on the realised \widehat{G}=\tau G — the Dirac-type equation. The Lean witness QOU.Mass.binding_qdifference_recurrence packages the depth-d recurrence as a structure and extracts the term identity; the existence of R for the binding G is the conjectural input (carried as the structure hypothesis). \qquad\blacksquare
